The words

Savior, like a shepherd lead us,
much we need Thy tender care;
In Thy pleasant pastures feed us,
for our use Thy folds prepare.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

We are Thine, Thou dost befriend us,
be the guardian of our way;
Keep Thy flock, from sin defend us,
seek us when we go astray.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.

Thou hast promised to receive us,
poor and sinful though we be;
Thou hast mercy to relieve us,
grace to cleanse and pow'r to free.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
We will early turn to Thee.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
We will early turn to Thee.

Early let us seek Thy favor,
early let us do Thy will;
Blessèd Lord and only Savior,
with Thy love our bosoms fill.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on m (G).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The words are by Dorothy Ann Thrupp, first published in 1836. The tune, BRADBURY, is by William Batchelder Bradbury (1859). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.

  • Words (1836): Dorothy Ann Thrupp (1779–1847)
  • Music (1859): William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868)

Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune BRADBURY by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by Dorothy Ann Thrupp (1779–1847). Questions about Savior, Like a Shepherd Lead Us

What is the doh of Savior, Like a Shepherd Lead Us?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Savior, Like a Shepherd Lead Us start on?

It starts on m (G in Eb major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

Is Savior, Like a Shepherd Lead Us in the public domain?

Yes. Dorothy Ann Thrupp died in 1847, William Batchelder Bradbury died in 1868; the words were first published in 1836 and the music in 1859. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
